messages:
jess: Seeing a spike of provisioning failures in eu-west-1 — warm-pool nodes keep failing init with decryption errors. Anyone else?
liam: yep, I'm seeing the same in the autoscaler logs. failures hit ~12% of requests in the last 10m.
maya: alert from deploy-bot just before the spike: `node-init: decrypt failed (AccessDenied)`.
deploy-bot: [infra] Instance i-0bbf.. stuck in INIT, reason: KMSAccessDenied. Auto-retry queued.
oliver: did we roll a keystore/IAM condition recently? security pushed a scoped key change this morning.
jess: @oliver could be it — we merged that policy change that tightened cross-account decrypt conditions.
maya: copying relevant snippet from node-init logs:
```
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z node-init: fetching /etc/secret-bootstrap -> calling KMS.Decrypt
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z KMS.Decrypt returned AccessDenied for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:222:alias/redwood-keystore
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z node-init: aborting boot, returning non-zero
```
liam: interestingly, US regions unaffected — they fall back to on-demand pools, which is adding cost. overnight spike in on-demand GPU usage ~2.2x.
jess: can we confirm whether the new policy added `Condition: StringEquals: aws:PrincipalAccount`? that would block our infra role if it's coming from the provisioning account.
oliver: yes, policy change: `AllowDecrypt` limited to `PrincipalAccount: 3333333333`. Looks like provisioning uses a different service account in eu.
security-bot: Policy deploy 2026-03-20T08:03:00: changed kms:Decrypt allow list -> restricted-accounts. Ticket SEC-4201.
liam: ok — temporary mitigation options? revert policy, add the infra principal, or change node-init to use a different keystore path.
maya: reverting is fastest. but we need audit trail — operations prefers adding the infra principal to the new policy instead of full revert.
jess: adding the infra principal needs cross-account grant. who owns the keystore alias in eu?
oliver: team-security owns the alias; I can add the infra role but need justification and time to run through approvals.
liam: meanwhile, eu warm pool is unhealthy. autoscaler is launching in other regions -> headroom drop and request queueing for region-local customers. cost team flagged a daily $/GPU jump.
jess: can we enable a small emergency grace: allow our infra role for kms:Decrypt via a temporary IAM statement for 30m, logged to audit, while oliver adds the permanent grant?
oliver: I can push a temporary statement now: `Condition: DateLessThan: 2026-03-20T10:00:00Z` + allow for role arn:aws:iam::444444444444:role/infra-provisioner.
maya: please also whitelist the autoscaler agent `arn:aws:sts::444444444444:assumed-role/autoscaler/*`. those are what actually call KMS during node init.
oliver: noted, will add both.
security-bot: Temporary policy added by oliver at 2026-03-20T09:18:12Z (expires 2026-03-20T10:00:00Z). Audit event ID: a1b2c3d4.
maya: node-init retries started to succeed for new jobs. warm-pool draining -> healthy again.
liam: seeing provisioning success rate jump back from 88% -> 99% in eu-west-1 after the temporary change.
jess: cost impact: finance says fallback on-demand during the 40m window added ~€1.4k in GPU run costs. we need to capture that in the post-incident notes.
oliver: permanent fix in flight: update keystore policy to include infra principals for region-local accounts, and add a cross-account grant doc. I'll open a PR and schedule a 30-min security review.
liam: ops action items: (1) confirm all warm-pool node roles included (2) add unit test that simulates KMS.Decrypt AccessDenied in CI (3) add monitoring alert that ties KMS AccessDenied spikes to provisioning SRs.
jess: also add an alert for sudden regional fallback to non-preferred regions (we missed that metric chain).
maya: filing incident in the tracker with logs + audit IDs.
oliver: one more note — unrelated but correlated: egress firewall tightening in eu this morning caused NAT gateway queueing spikes. some init retries showed `ERR_NET_UNREACHABLE` before Decrypt errors. we should verify whether the network rules caused some nodes to hit different execution paths.
jess: good catch. @liam can you correlate egress firewall change timeframe with the KMS errors?
liam: on it. early signal looks: firewall change at 08:55, KMS policy deploy at 08:03, failures spike from 09:06 onward. might be compounded by both.
maya: summary for the incident writeup: root cause = overly-restrictive keystore policy rollout + regional firewall changes -> provisioning retries, fallback to on-demand -> cost spike. mitigation = temporary policy grant + PR for permanent grant + firewall rule sanity check.
jess: thanks everyone. I'll own the postmortem and include cost tags and audit IDs.
liam: adding recommended playbook entry: before KMS/keystore policy changes, run a region-local node-init dry-run using the infra role.
oliver: PR opened: github.com/redwood/sec/keystore-policy#487. assigned to oliver, target patch in 3 hours.
maya: closing the thread once postmortem links are in. :white_check_mark:
